Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes. The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. stories.summary: The 4-0 debacle against Switzerland has added to the tactical concerns about the head coach’s suitability, just six games into the job The Scottish Football Association can only cling to a lesson from the past when assessing a worrying international window. Steve Clarke was beleaguered during his early games in charge. Successive 4-0 defeats by Belgium and Russia in 2019 left Clarke with the sense he should have stayed in club management. A revival meant Clarke led his country to three out of four tournaments. There are, however, fundamental differences between the story of Clarke and that being delivered by Sébastien Pocognoli. stories.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
stories.summary: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managers Sign up for our free newsletter here Who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom S Although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling. items.title: Spain in pain as historic run ends but De la Fuente feels best is yet to come
items.summary: While the head coach, players and Spanish press were magnanimous in defeat, there was pride mixed in with disappointment – and confidence the future is still bright “With every game, defeat gets closer,” Luis de la Fuente had said and on Sunday night it finally came. Spain had lost only one competitive game since Scotland in March 2023 back when the coach hadn’t won anything and didn’t look like he ever would – and that solitary loss was on penalties in the 2025 Nations League final . Statistically, they said, penalties don’t count, so while Portugal lifted the trophy that night, the team that won the European Championship and World Cup in the summers either side also claimed a Fifa record of 44 official games unbeaten. And then England turned up at the Metropolitano . A night that started with Iker Casillas, Fernando Torres and Fernando Llorente handing the World Cup to Unai Simón ended with Spain trying to overhaul a shock 3-0 deficit. Against 10 men and led by a superb Lamine Yamal, Spain made De la Fuente think for a while that they would too, but it wasn’t to be. Continue reading...

items.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
items.summary: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managers Sign up for our free newsletter here Who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom S Although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling. items.summary: The 4-0 debacle against Switzerland has added to the tactical concerns about the head coach’s suitability, just six games into the job The Scottish Football Association can only cling to a lesson from the past when assessing a worrying international window. Steve Clarke was beleaguered during his early games in charge. Successive 4-0 defeats by Belgium and Russia in 2019 left Clarke with the sense he should have stayed in club management. A revival meant Clarke led his country to three out of four tournaments. There are, however, fundamental differences between the story of Clarke and that being delivered by Sébastien Pocognoli. Clarke was a pragmatist, whose decades in coaching suggested he had the wherewithal to revive Scotland. Pocognoli, six games into his tenure, is in danger of lurching into the territory of dreamy ideologue whose aspiration for how Scotland must play is unworkable. items.title: Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes

Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes. The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based.
